links.outcome: Grading of chatbot answers to complex chronic venous disease questions by two specialists
links.effect: ChatGPT 4.0 grade 1 on 15/20 (75%), grade 4 on 1/20 (5%); ChatGPT 3.5 grade 1 on 9/20 (45%), grade 4 on 3/20 (15%); Clinical Camel grade 1 on 0/20, grade 4 on 10/20 (50%).
links.quote: Clinical Camel received a grade of 1 on 0 of 20 questions (0%), grade 2 on 5 of 20 questions (25%), grade 3 on 5 of 20 questions (25%), and grade 4 on 10 of 20 questions (50%).

links.outcome: Comparison of candidate chatbots on identical questions graded by specialists
links.effect: ChatGPT 4.0 outperformed ChatGPT 3.5 on administrative questions (20/20 grade 1 vs 14/20, 70%) and on complex questions (75% vs 45% grade 1); Clinical Camel performed worst (0% grade 1).
links.quote: On administrative and non-complex medical questions, ChatGPT 4.0 performed better than ChatGPT 3.5.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests LLMs (ChatGPT 3.5, ChatGPT 4.0, Clinical Camel) on administrative and complex medical queries related to chronic venous disease to assess their accuracy for inbox management, but evaluates model performance alone without testing specific deployment safeguards.
